answer.evidence: The ambulance is a flat side elevation facing west, with wheels, a red stripe and a cross on the body side. The box body has a pale band at rows 12-16, but it fades into the side face at row 17 with no front-edge line (the nearest line, row 24, sits well inside the side face) and no eave shadow. It reads as a highlight on a curved roofline, not a horizontal roof surface. The cab roof and windshield follow the same pattern, so no part shows a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ambulance is a clean, readable vehicle, but its shading is shallow. The white body has about 3 steps (white, light grey, grey-blue shadow) and the large side panel is a mostly flat white area with no grain or panel texture. The measured near-flat coverage is 24%, higher than every reference (0-13%). Visible tones per tile are 9, equal to the hedge but well below the stall (17) and well (20), which are the richer same-kind references. The outline is dark and bluish-grey with a slight tint (0% neutral edge pixels), so it is not a pure black sticker line. It is selective around the cab and wheels, but the bottom and wheels read as a uniform dark rim. The flat white body panel, the thin roof and window shading, and the lack of per-material texture (no grain, speckle or dirt) make it flatter than the stall and well.

answer.evidence: The ambulance is drawn in west-facing side profile. Rows 12-16 form a near-white roof band (L=234) across both the cab and the box, which is lighter than the grey body (L=186) from row 17 down. That is a 5-row top surface. It has no sharp front-edge line and no eave shadow, so the evidence is weak. The roof band is followed by a large south face of about 25 rows (17-41): a crease at row 24, a red cross, a red stripe at rows 35-37 and wheels reaching row 47. The top is thin but present on both cab and box.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ambulance is a clean, readable van with a white body, a red cross, a grey bumper and dark wheels. The body is mostly large flat white/light-grey panels with only about 3-4 steps, a thin shading band along the bottom and some window highlights. The measured near-flat coverage is 24%, higher than every reference (0-13%), and the candidate has 9 visible tones per tile, which matches the hedge but is well below the stall (17) and well (20). The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean toward a tinted dark blue-grey rather than a black sticker line, which is acceptable. It has little grain, panel detail or texture dots on the body, so it looks flatter than the stall and well. The vehicle is a larger flat-sided form than the references, which makes the flat white panels more noticeable. A careful artist would likely ask for more shading steps and surface texture on the roof and side before accepting it next to the stall and well.

answer.evidence: The ambulance faces west, so its south face is the side profile (rows 17-41, about 25 rows, with the red stripe, cross and wheels). Above it, rows 12-16 form a distinctly lighter roof band (L=234 against about 186 on the side) over the whole length. The silhouette also narrows toward the top, from 90 wide at row 30 to 59 at row 11, which suggests a curved roof. The band has no 1-row front-edge line and no eave shadow, so the roof evidence is weak. It is still a deliberate roof plane about 5 rows tall, not a 1-2 row rim, so I read it as a top surface and call the drawing three_quarter.

This confirms big flat areas on the white box and the long side panel. It has 9 visible tones per tile, which matches the hedge but is well below the stall (17) and the well (20). answer.evidence: The ambulance faces west and shows its own side as the south face. The cargo box has a pale roof band in rows 12-16 (L=234). Its silhouette widens from 59 to 74 px across rows 11-16, so the roof edges are rounded. At row 17 the colour steps down to the grey side panel (L=186), but this is a lightness step, not a distinct 1-row edge line, and there is no eave shadow, so the top-surface evidence is weak. The side wall runs from row 17 to about row 41 and carries a body-molding line at row 24, a red cross, and a red stripe at rows 35-37. The cab has a similar pale roof area above the windshield and side window. Wheels and the siren lights on top of the cab roof add detail. Both parts have a roof band above a tall vertical face, so I read it as three_quarter.
